instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil for the noodles.
Meanwhile, slice the mushrooms about 1/4 inch thick and slice the onion. Mince the 3 garlic cloves. Cut the scallions into 1 inch pieces, keeping the whites and greens apart.
In a small bowl, stir together 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp vegan oyster sauce, 2 tsp sugar, 1 tsp sesame oil and 1/4 cup water. This is the sauce.
Cook the noodles in the boiling water for 1 minute less than the package says. Drain them, rinse them under cold water and shake off as much water as you can.

Heat a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil, then half the mushrooms in a single layer and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Leave them alone for 2 minutes, until the underside is golden.
Stir the mushrooms and cook for 2 minutes, until they're browned all over. Transfer them to a plate.

Add 1 tbsp of the oil to the same pan, then the rest of the mushrooms and the last 1/4 tsp salt. Cook them the same way, 2 minutes untouched, then stir and cook for 2 minutes. Transfer them to the plate.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil to the pan with the onion and the scallion whites. Stir for 2 minutes, until the onion softens and starts to brown at the edges.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Add the noodles. Stir the sauce, pour it over and toss with tongs for 2 minutes, until the noodles are hot and coated.
Return the mushrooms and any juices to the pan. Add the bean sprouts and the scallion greens and toss for 30 seconds. Take the pan off the heat.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash more soy sauce.
Serve in bowls, sprinkled with the sesame seeds.
method_notes: No version of this dish has 20 ratings (Oh My Veg 1, Loving It Vegan 6, Nutriciously 16), and RecipeTin Eats has only a chicken chow mein, so this leads with Oh My Veg, the one built around seared mushrooms. All the versions toss boiled noodles with a soy and vegan oyster sauce; Loving It Vegan adds peppers, carrot and broth, and Supper in the Suburbs adds bean sprouts and crisps the noodles. Scaled up from the lead's 200 g of mushrooms and noodles to fill four bowls, with vegan noodles (check the label, some are made with egg) and vegan oyster sauce.
